hedges.reason: E51 pays if the Houthis actually hit or seize a commercial ship. For the Houthis to reach Aden, the Saudi-backed front in the south would have to collapse and the Houthis would be pushing their advantage. In that world, they have both more room and more reason to use maritime pressure near Bab el-Mandeb, and this is the listed instrument closest to that effect.

If the Houthis hold ground on both sides of the approaches to Bab el-Mandeb, insurers and shipping lines would divert traffic around the Cape. Transit counts at the strait would fall toward the PortWatch closure threshold. This expresses the shipping-diversion part of the hedge thesis.

Red Sea export routes, including Saudi shipments out of Yanbu, would carry a higher risk premium. That premium would show up in crude prices, expressing the energy part of the thesis. Iran and Hormuz news would also move this price, so it is only a partial expression.

claims.reason: A Houthi ground push into Aden by the end of October would mean open war with the Saudi-backed camp and the collapse of the effective de-escalation. The Houthis have repeatedly used strikes on commercial shipping as leverage and signalling during escalations. I do not think the Houthis would take Aden in the same window while holding back entirely from hitting commercial shipping, so these two outcomes are unlikely to happen together.
